name: Aruba
summary_text: Aruba: autonomous country within the Kingdom; Charter equality framework; Catholic community norms; tourism economy. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: Netherlands (0.79) plus a local delta of -0.08. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Safety and travel information - Pride Amsterdam 2027
sources.claim_summary: WorldPride Amsterdam 2026 safety and travel page (about the Netherlands, included here as regional context). Covers entry/border procedures, Schengen passport-carrying rules, Schiphol airport logistics, taxi safety, and general city caution, with a dedicated section for transgender and non-binary visitors. Notes the Netherlands ranks #13 on the ILGA Rainbow Map 2026.

sources.title: Netherlands | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for the Netherlands (updated March 2026): same-sex relations legal, marriage and adoption available, legal gender recognition possible but still requires an expert letter from a medical professional; nonbinary 'X' marker only via a court procedure taking 3-9 months; the Transgender Act (which would have introduced self-ID) was withdrawn by the government in July 2025. Relevant to Aruba as a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

sources.title: Aruba - Gay and LGBT Friendly Caribbean Travel Destination
sources.claim_summary: Aruba's official tourism website LGBT vacations page: markets Aruba ('One Happy Island') as welcoming to all visitors, with nearly 100 nationalities living together; general tourism promotion with an LGBT-specific landing page.

sources.title: Aruba Votes for LGBT Civil Union as first Island in the Caribbean
sources.claim_summary: Aruba's official tourism site news item: Aruba voted for LGBT civil unions as the first island in the Caribbean - official promotion of the island's LGBT-inclusive development.

sources.title: Gay Life in a Tolerant Society in Aruba - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz travel-culture report (2017): 'Gay Life in a Tolerant Society in Aruba' - describes the ABC islands (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao) as quiet nests of gay-friendliness within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, with a tolerant and mostly open society; travel-oriented first-person perspective.

sources.title: Aruba Parliament approves civil unions for same-sex couples
sources.claim_summary: AP via Yahoo (Sept 2016): Aruba's parliament voted 11-5 (4 abstentions) to grant same-sex couples the right to register unions and receive benefits granted to married people (spousal pension, emergency medical decisions); previously couples married in the Netherlands could have certificates recognised; MP Desiree de Sousa Croes noted many islanders oppose same-sex unions on religious and cultural grounds.
